sphere_commentary.overview:
The dataset shows strong aggregate efficacy across all three series with means clustered between 6.5-7.0.
• HEALING protocols lead in consistency and sample size (n=574), with DESCENT structures performing as expected for nervous system regulation.
• THRIVING series achieves highest mean scores within its Focus & Clarity subgroup (T-FC-L3: 7.63), validating HOLD structure for cognitive optimisation.
• TRANSFORMING shows structurally expected higher variance (std=1.87) due to low-affect listener states, with ASCENT protocols revealing optimization opportunities.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The three series demonstrate differentiated efficacy patterns aligned with their design intents.
• HEALING shows the strongest aggregate signal with lowest variance across DESCENT protocols, particularly excelling in Over-stimulation (H-OS-L1: mean 7.15, n=95).
• THRIVING validates its HOLD structure through high Focus & Clarity outcomes (T-FC-L3: 7.63), while Creative Flow protocols lag slightly behind expectations.
• TRANSFORMING's ASCENT protocols show mixed results with higher variance, as expected for low-affect listener populations, suggesting protocol-specific refinements rather than series-level issues.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols show significant deviations from expected patterns that warrant investigation.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean=5.70, std=2.45) presents the lowest mean and highest variance in TRANSFORMING, with bimodal distribution risk.
• AutoGluon predicted vs observed deltas: X-ME-L1 predicted 8.230 but observed 6.74; H-CR-L2 predicted 7.955 but observed 6.52 - both suggest VOL001 groove limitations.
• T-FC-L3 shows high cross-run drift (sim=0.532) despite strong outcome, indicating analytical uncertainty that may affect interpretation.
• Embedding drift analysis reveals 29 protocols with sim < 0.85, suggesting evolving data patterns or genuine analytical instability.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Multiple convergent opportunities emerge for protocol optimization based on quantitative and qualitative signals.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-ME-L1: Predicted as optimal (8.230) but observed moderate (6.74) - revise adviser routing to increase exposure since AutoGluon detects strong latent efficacy.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-OS-L1: Highest performing protocol (n=95, mean=7.15) - develop L2/L3 variants to test WING RATIO adjustments for overstimulation entrainment.
• H-CR-L2: AutoGluon's top crisis prediction (7.955) but observed 6.52 - investigate VOL001 groove mismatch through music opinion split (38% neutral).
• T-FC-L3: Highest THRIVING mean (7.63) with AutoGluon confirmation (7.728) - test extended hold phase for deeper entrainment given 15/29 settle at 10 minutes.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run semantic analysis reveals moderate analytical instability across protocols.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: X-MD-L3 shows highest drift (sim=0.507) indicating significant interpretive shift; 13 protocols have sim < 0.6 suggesting evolving data patterns.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: Sleep protocols form tight cluster (H-SL-L1 ↔ H-SL-L2: 0.869), while H-OS-L3 is most analytically distinct (mean_sim=0.677).
• Confidence note: Drift spans 18-90 days with limited historical runs; earlier runs had lower n contributing to instability.
• Panel divided on interpretation: Three analyzers flag drift as concerning, two treat it as expected data evolution.

by_protocol.X-ME-L1: n=39, mean=6.74, std=1.94, confidence=meaningful. AutoGluon ranks across ALL zones highest at 8.230, especially for low-affect states - strong latent efficacy detected. Music split 27% neutral. Cross-run drift sim=0.818 indicates commentary stability despite prediction-outcome gap. YouTube: 8 views.
by_protocol.X-ME-L2: n=25, mean=6.76, std=1.71, confidence=meaningful. 20% find rhythm slightly busy. Moderate settle (4/15 at 20 min / 4 immediate). Cross-run drift sim=0.532 significant. YouTube: 8 views.
by_protocol.X-ME-L3: n=18, mean=6.28, std=1.74, confidence=developing. 28% (5/25) report no effect - high non-response. Rhythm balanced. Small n. Cross-run drift sim=0.627. YouTube: 4 views.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Most people using this for anxiety feel noticeably calmer, typically within about 10 minutes. Works well whether you're in therapy, driving, or just need to decompress.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Helps with anxiety for many, though a few people felt neutral about the music. Works best during commutes or therapy sessions.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Good for anxiety relief but takes longer to settle in. Mixed views on how calming the rhythm feels - works for some, less so for others.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Used during crisis or acute distress - many report significant improvement within 5-10 minutes. Music liked but not loved. A small number felt no effect.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Calms people in crisis for many, though the music doesn't click for everyone. Works during both work and sleep attempts.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Settles people very quickly - important for acute situations. But the rhythm isn't universally liked, with some finding it not to their taste.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Our strongest performer for overstimulation - most people notice meaningful improvement and settle within 10 minutes. Well-liked musically.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Calming for many during relaxation or commutes. Some people remained neutral about the music, but rhythm helped them settle.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Popular when people are trying to sleep - about a third of users chose it for that. Responses on rhythm are mixed - some find it busy.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Helps wind down fairly quickly for sleep, with a strong satisfaction rate. Music is well-liked and it's consistent for rest.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Used during study or driving but might be too active for some sleep situations. A notable portion found the rhythm too busy.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Good for relaxation and caregiver support, but for some it doesn't help them settle. Mixed feedback on the rhythm.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Gives a slight to moderate boost for creative work. Reactions to the music are mixed - loved by some, neutral for others.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Well-liked musically and helps creativity, especially during commutes or when trying to fall asleep. Takes about 10 minutes to take effect.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Many people experience significant creative improvement, even when using it during sleep. Music appreciated though rhythm isn't universal.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Provides mild to moderate focus support. Some find the rhythm a bit too active for deep concentration.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Helps with focus over time but not instantly. Music opinions are split - some love it, others are neutral.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Best in the focus category - strong results with many people loving the music and finding it motivating for various tasks.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Takes longer to work (around 20 minutes for many) but helps maintain balance. Best suited for therapy or extended listening sessions.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Mixed results - some found it helpful for work or sleep, others felt the rhythm was too busy for their needs.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Helps many but a notable portion didn't settle at all. Music is okay but the rhythm doesn't click for everyone.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Helps mental clarity for most, though a small number (2 out of 25) said it actually made things worse. Most loved the music.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Works quickly and is well-liked - helps many gain mental clarity, especially during study or relaxation.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Results are inconsistent - some benefit, others don't. A few found the rhythm too intense. Small sample makes conclusions tentative.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Boosts motivation for some, but results are hit-or-miss. Works best during study or relaxation periods.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Slow to take effect (often 20 minutes) but helpful for some during study or sleep. Many loved the music.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Works well for some with low energy, though not a universal fit. Positive that it settles people relatively quickly.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Designed to improve mood, and our models predict it should work very well - though actual results are only moderate so far.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Helps some feel better over time, though it's not immediate. Music is generally well-liked.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Mixed results - some feel better, others see no change at all. Useful during relaxation or light tasks.
